pages.title: Plate information management software
text: Plate information management is a proposed software product in its own right. Laboratories and research groups may need reliable plate records even when their images come from different instruments. PIMS should provide a stable identity and provenance model across those acquisition sources.

The software should organize plate associations, observations, analysis versions, quality decisions and review states. Search should answer operational questions such as which records need review, which images used a superseded calibration and which exports remain unacknowledged. Retrieval should not depend on a staff member remembering a file naming convention.

PIMS should integrate with the laboratory’s authoritative patient and order systems rather than create unnecessary duplicate identity stores. The appropriate source of truth for each field must be agreed during integration. A research deployment may use study identifiers and require no patient details at all.

The initial product value can be evaluated through successful retrieval, identity consistency, correction completeness and reviewer usability. Predictive features can be added later without changing the meaning of the original observation record. The detailed PIMS chapter and interface appendices define the proposed record relationships and expected handling of measured, derived, imputed, simulated and unavailable values.

pages.title: Analysis and decision support software
text: Analysis software converts observations into candidate measurements and reviewable evidence. Decision support adds context that helps a qualified user understand the result. These functions should be distinguished from autonomous clinical decision-making and from the deterministic application of an eligible standards rule.

The proposed software combines conventional image processing, task-specific learned models and explicit quality logic. A geometric method may be sufficient for one measurement, while a learned model may help with variable appearance or ambiguous segmentation. Every AI capability should be compared with a simpler baseline and judged by its effect on the intended workflow.

An explanation should identify what affected the result and what the user can do next. A coloured overlay may help locate a boundary, but it does not establish that the algorithm used a biologically valid feature. A confidence score should have a defined empirical meaning and should be evaluated on representative data. [R21] [R22]

The product should make uncertainty actionable through review, additional observation or abstention. It should also preserve a record of overrides so that developers can investigate recurring weaknesses. Human review is most useful when the interface exposes the evidence needed for independent judgement, rather than simply asking the user to confirm an automated answer.

pages.title: Laboratory connectivity products
text: Connectivity products should move laboratory information with its meaning intact. The challenge is not only transmitting a value; it is preserving identity, units, method, status, version and correction semantics across systems that may use different conventions.
## Define a mapping before an interface

Each integration needs a field-level agreement between the sending and receiving systems. The agreement should identify authoritative identifiers, required terminology, permitted result states and acknowledgement behaviour. Common messaging standards can support that agreement, but they do not remove the need for site-specific mapping and verification.

A successful network request does not prove that a result reached the correct record. The product should reconcile acknowledgements and expose unresolved exports. Duplicate submissions should be idempotent where the receiving interface supports that behaviour. When a destination cannot represent a required field, the limitation should be resolved through the approved workflow rather than by dropping the field silently.

Connectivity can be offered as adapters, supported integrations and partner interfaces. Each should carry a compatibility statement and a conformance test set. Changes in a laboratory information system, terminology dictionary or result schema should trigger a review of the integration evidence, even when the instrument’s measurement software has not changed.
